title: Infineon’s PSOC™ Control C3 Performance Line sets new standard for real-time control and PQC security Technology news Sep 22, 2026
content_text:
Infineon’s PSOC™ Control C3 Performance Line sets new standard for real-time control and PQC security 
Technology news
Sep 22, 2026 
Munich, Germany – 22 September 2026 – Infineon Technologies AG (FSE: IFX / OTCQX: IFNNY) today announced the launch of its PSOC™ Control C3 Performance Line microcontroller family to enable real-time control for power and motor applications. The new family of microcontrollers (MCUs) offers best-in-class performance through high control loop frequency, accuracy and system efficiency. Based on Arm® Cortex®-M33 multi-core architecture, PSOC Control C3 Performance Line MCUs meet the needs of applications that require precise, high-speed control for power conversion such as AI server PSUs, solar, SMPS, EV charging or high-end motor control. 
The MCUs are compliant with Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) requirements for firmware protection outlined in the Commercial National Security Algorithm (CNSA) Suite 2.0. In addition, the MCUs support PSA (Platform Security Architecture) Level 3 enablement. By supporting both standards, Infineon’s PSOC Control C3 Performance Line meets the security needs for a wide range of industrial applications and eases their transition to increased security in the post-quantum cryptography era. 
“The family is designed for digital control applications that need higher switching frequencies while providing precision, security and maximum system efficiency,” said Steve Tateosian, SVP and General Manager, IoT, Consumer and Industrial MCUs, Infineon Technologies. “As the industry shifts from analog to digital control for power conversion and motor control applications, and world prepares for PQC era, the PSOC Control C3 Performance Line meets these needs for increased performance, system flexibility, security and scalability without increasing the footprint.” 
Key features and benefits 
Arm Cortex-M33-based microcontrollers with up to 180 MHz 
PPCA hardware accelerator with dual-Arm Cortex-M33-based microcontrollers with up to 200 MHz, zero wait state fast analog and digital peripherals access to enable high-performance systems to respond to real-time events with minimal delay 
Provides a high level of functional integration for multiple-output power supply
Wide-bandgap-ready with fast, precise analog processing and digital control to improve control loop accuracy and system efficiency
Low standby power for battery powered application
Scalable and compatible portfolio in features, packages, pinouts, memory and performance
Quicker time-to-market with ModusToolbox™ Power Suite and Motor Suite GUI as a unified and comprehensive software and ecosystem platform for developers with dedicated tools and advanced libraries 
Up to PSA L3 / EPC3 security incl. PQC support and “DICE ready”
Enable secured on-site and cloud-based systems with secured boot, secured FW update, code protection, secured identifier for attestation, secured key storage ready, authenticity and integrity protection
About PSOC Control C3 family 
The PSOC Control C3 family of MCUs provide real-time control for motor control and power conversion applications. New MCUs of the PSOC Control C3 Performance Line enable system performance at high switching frequencies and increase control loop bandwidth. That is achieved with proprietary autonomous hardware accelerators as well as high resolution and high performing analog peripheral support. The family supports systems designed with wide-bandgap switches while achieving best-in-class control loop frequencies, accuracy and efficiency for applications such as data centers, telecom, solar, and electric vehicle (EV) charging systems. 
Availability 
Samples of the PSOC Control C3 Performance Line with Post-Quantum Cryptography compliance are available now. The CNSA 2.0-compatible MCU family includes SHA-512 and LMS firmware verification for secured boot and firmware update verification. Infineon offers dedicated parts for Power Conversion (PSC3P8/PSC3P7) and Motor Control (PSC3M8/PSC3M7) with multiple package options with up to 100 pins. ModusToolbox Power Suite and Motor Suite provide a design environment including control libraries and tools. 
For more information on PSOC Control MCUs, visit http://www.infineon.com/psoccontrolc3performanceline . For more information on Infineon’s PQC solutions, visit www.infineon.com/PQC .
About Infineon
Infineon Technologies AG is a global semiconductor leader in power systems and IoT. Infineon drives decarbonization and digitalization with its products and solutions. The Company had around 57,000 employees worldwide (end of September 2025) and generated revenue of about €14.7 billion in the 2025 fiscal year (ending 30 September). Infineon is listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange (ticker symbol: IFX) and in the USA on the OTCQX International over-the-counter market (ticker symbol: IFNNY).

title: Computational Chemistry and AI in Chemistry Conference at Headquarters in Darmstadt
content_text:
Computational Chemistry and AI in Chemistry Conference at Headquarters in Darmstadt 
We have hosted one of the largest conferences focusing on computational chemistry and AI in chemistry with around 300 participants in Darmstadt. 
Subscribe
Share 
Icons revealed to the left 
21 Sep 2026 
| 
Darmstadt, Germany 
RDKit conference with more than 300 participants 
Applications of open-source cheminformatics and machine learning tool expand from small molecules to oligonucleotides, peptides and quantum chemistry 
Conference celebrates 20 th birthday of RDKit and highlights examples of scientific expertise being turned into applications 
Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, a leading science and technology company, has hosted one of the largest conferences focusing on computational chemistry and AI in chemistry, bringing together a global community of chemists, data scientists and software developers. All attendees share the common goal of making precompetitive molecular research faster, more reliable and more collaborative. Around 300 participants met in Darmstadt, half of them in person, the other half virtually.
“RDKit is a powerful example of how chemistry, data and software can come together to accelerate scientific innovation. We are proud to welcome the RDKit community to Darmstadt and to support the shared foundations that help turn scientific expertise into impact,” said Philipp Harbach, Chief Science and Technology Officer at Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany.
The agenda for the 2026 meeting of prestigious digital chemistry experts shows that the applications of RDKit , originally developed to handle small molecules, have expanded to include promising modalities such as oligonucleotides and peptides as well as quantum chemistry. Contributions from Novartis, Bayer, Sanofi, and AbbVie, among others, highlight the importance of RDKit as a key toolkit for pharmaceutical research. “RDKit helps our research and development scientists within our Healthcare business sector turn chemical data into AI-ready representations and actionable insights for faster, better-informed molecular design. By supporting its open-source community, we help advance shared tools that enable us to bring more medicines to more patients, faster,” said Arvind Rajpal, Head of Discovery & Development Technologies at Research and Development within the Healthcare business sector of Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany.
RDKit is an important open-source cheminformatics and machine learning tool that has more than 100,000 users worldwide. The open-source software helps scientists represent, analyze and compare molecules in a computer – giving digital tools a common language for chemical structures. Researchers can use it to check molecular structures, look for similarities between compounds and prepare chemical data for modeling.
The software is now an important building block in many chemistry- and life science-focused AI workflows. It helps turn the rich but complex information contained in molecular structures into data that models can use – supporting scientists as they identify promising molecules, estimate properties and design the next experiments.
Examples of digital science projects at Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, using RDKit are:
Predictive Modeling Platform , a tool for AI-driven design of drug-like molecules for the Healthcare business sector, recently recognized with an in-house award at Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany
Protein Design Platform , a suite of protein AI tools developed at the Science & Technology Office at Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, recognized with an award by Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany in 2025
BayBE , a Bayesian optimization tool by the Science & Technology Office at Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, that helps teams choose informative follow-up experiments, recognized with a Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany in-house award in 2025
Synthia ® , an externally available retrosynthesis product from the Life Science business sector of Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, that helps chemists explore practical routes for synthesizing a target molecule
These tools address different scientific questions, from deciding which experiment to run next to planning how a molecule could be made or can show how drug candidates interact with proteins.
However, RDKit is used much more broadly in digital tools. Pharmaceutical and chemical companies also use RDKit to develop digital tools in-house. Google (Patents) and Google DeepMind (AlphaFold), Amazon Web Services and NVIDIA use RDKit alongside chemical supplier Enamine and software provider Schrödinger.
RDKit began with its first open-source publication in 2006 as a company-developed project and has grown into a widely used open-source toolkit with almost 4 million downloads per month and an expanding international community. Google Scholar had more than 4,500 hits for “RDKit” in 2024 alone. Its value is in the software and community itself, and in the way it enables scientists in academia, technology companies and the pharmaceutical industry to learn from one another. When companies share methods, code and experience responsibly, the wider scientific community moves faster.
Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany has been part of the RDKit community since its earliest days. The first and then still very small RDKit User Group Meeting was in 2012 with Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany employees contributing. In 2014, Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany hosted the third User Group Meeting in Darmstadt with several contributions. By welcoming this community to Darmstadt for the 20 th anniversary, Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany is celebrating the RDKit community’s open-source progress and helping shape the next generation of digital chemistry. “Hosting this community at our headquarters offers a valuable opportunity to exchange ideas and strengthen collaboration across industry, academia and open-source contributors. We are proud to support this spirit of openness and innovation – because the future of science depends on connecting people, data and technology,” said Jérémie Eblé, Head of Digital Center of Excellence at the Life Science business sector of Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany.

content_text:

It is easy to see why ruthenium is considered a critical raw material of high strategic value. Found in only the tiniest amounts and in just a few regions, this metal has special properties with a powerful impact across multiple uses. For one of the rarest metals on Earth, ruthenium certainly punches above its weight.
A small amount of this element can have a transformative effect, from dramatically increasing a product’s hardness, durability and wear-resistance, to enabling highly complex chemical reactions.
Ruthenium is the hidden champion of the platinum group metals (PGMs), with metallurgical, technical, electrotechnical properties. Just a little ruthenium can have a big impact.
Joachim Grimm, Sales Manager for Umicore’s Metal Deposition Solutions
Special qualities
That impact often comes down to ruthenium’s hardness and how it behaves in coatings. It is applied in fine grains to create wear-resistant layers and can also be added to harden softer, precious metal surfaces. In jewelry and accessories, even small additions can significantly improve a product’s lifetime. As Joachim notes: “Adding just 5% of ruthenium to an alloy can make a piece last two or three times longer.” 
Ruthenium’s unique qualities are also helping to advance electronics by enabling the continued miniaturization of microchips. As chips get ever smaller, the materials inside them are packed more tightly, making it increasingly difficult to prevent damage or interference – through corrosion, atomic diffusion, or the migration of metals between layers. As Joachim explains, an ultra-thin layer of ruthenium applied to materials in the microchip forms a “perfect corrosion and diffusion barrier” , helping to maintain the integrity and performance of microchips as they get smaller.
Choreographing chemistry 
Beyond materials and electronics, ruthenium plays a standout role in chemistry. Christophe Le Ret, Director Business Development and Strategy for Umicore’s Precious Metals Chemistry, highlights its remarkable catalytic properties. “It’s one of the very few transition metals to be Nobel-prized, thanks to its unique qualities as a catalyst,” he says. 
In 2005, the scientists Robert Grubbs, Yves Chauvin and Richard Schrock were awarded the Nobel Prize for Chemistry for their role in unlocking the secrets of ‘metathesis’ – a chemical reaction in which molecules can be made to ‘switch partners’ to create new, more useful molecules. 
The choreographer of this molecular dance is ruthenium. As such, ruthenium-based ‘Grubbs catalysts’ enable complex chemical reactions that would otherwise be far more difficult. What’s more, reactions can be managed in a stable and predictable environment and with low waste. 
The impact is far-reaching. These catalysts have transformed how medicines, plastics, and advanced materials are made, supporting everything from polymers produced from renewable materials to new treatments for cancer, Alzheimer’s and HIV/AIDS. Ruthenium catalysts are also used in the production of flavors and fragrances. 
Scarcity and strategic supply 
Despite its wide range of applications, ruthenium’s strategic importance is shaped by its scarcity: it is not mined on its own but as a by-product of platinum and palladium, so supply cannot easily ramp up when demand spikes. 
Roughly 25 tonnes of ruthenium is mined annually. That makes it one of the smallest metal markets in the world. Visualized as a cube, it would measure only around 1.5 meters on all sides.
David Van Dijck, Manager Market Strategy and Business Development
Despite this extreme scarcity, there is strong demand for ruthenium for applications in electronics, data centers, AI and electrochemistry. According to Umicore Precious Metals Management Trader & Analyst Sven Bandilla, “tight supply and rapidly growing demand from the technology sector are driving significant volatility in ruthenium prices, which have hit new record highs several times in recent years.” 
Circularity is key 
When supply is constrained and prices swing, recycling becomes essential, not only for sustainability, but for security of supply. Umicore is one of the major recyclers and refiners of ruthenium, with materials returning through multiple streams, including spent catalysts, used electronics and industrial by-products. 
Recovered ruthenium is largely returned to the market, while a share is reintegrated into Umicore’s own value chains, supporting its circular model where materials are recycled, refined and reintroduced into production. 
In a world where such a small ingredient can unlock disproportionately impactful effects, circularity will play an increasingly important role for ruthenium, with Umicore’s expertise at the forefront. When a metal is this scarce and precious, the question of how it is managed, through recycling, collaboration, and efficient use, is just as important as the metal itself.

It is easy to see why ruthenium is considered a critical raw material of high strategic value. Found in only the tiniest amounts and in just a few regions, this metal has special properties with a powerful impact across multiple uses. For one of the rarest metals on Earth, ruthenium certainly punches above its weight.
A small amount of this element can have a transformative effect, from dramatically increasing a product’s hardness, durability and wear-resistance, to enabling highly complex chemical reactions.
Ruthenium is the hidden champion of the platinum group metals (PGMs), with metallurgical, technical, electrotechnical properties. Just a little ruthenium can have a big impact.
Joachim Grimm, Sales Manager for Umicore’s Metal Deposition Solutions

title: 長崎県で自動運転車の導入検討にAIを活用
source: DNP - Corporate News / Newsroom / News RSS
content_text:
長崎県で自動運転車の導入検討にAIを活用
実走行データから地域の危険場面や交通環境の特徴を分析・整理 
製品・サービス 
モビリティ 
AI 
地域創生・まちづくり 
コラボレーション 
大日本印刷株式会社（DNP）は、自動運転車の社会実装に向けて、車両の走行映像や位置情報などの実走行データをAIで分析し、自動運転車の導入検討に必要な情報を提供する「AI駆動型アセスメント」の取り組みを開始しました。その第一弾として、2026年9月から長崎県で実施している実証に活用しています。 
本実証は、長崎県の「自動運転車の社会実装に向けた長崎版AI診断手法の検証事業」をDNPが受託して実施するものです。本実証では、長崎県とDNPに加え、長崎県内の大学も含めた産官学連携のもと、「AI駆動型アセスメント」を活用して、長崎市などで収集する実走行データをもとに、危険場面や地域ごとの特徴などを分析し、2027年3月31日までに「長崎版AI診断手法」を検証します。
長崎の実証で検証する「AI駆動型アセスメント」の全体像
背景・事業のねらい 
自動運転技術では、周囲の状況を認識し、走行を判断・制御するために、車両におけるAIの活用が進んでいます。一方、自動運転車を地域で社会実装するためには、道路の形状や交通量、歩行者・自転車の動きなどを把握し、走行ルートや時間帯、運行・監視方法などの条件を検討する必要があります。 
DNPは、こうした自動運転車の導入条件を検討する場合にも、AIを活用できると考えました。AIが実走行データから地域ごとの危険場面や交通環境の特徴を分析し、自動運転車の導入条件を検討するための判断材料として活用します。DNPは自動運転車そのものを開発するのではなく、実世界から得られるデータをAIが利用できる形に整え、AIによる分析結果と人による確認を組み合わせて、導入検討に必要な情報を整理します。DNPは、この一連の取り組みを「AI駆動型アセスメント」と位置づけ、今回、長崎県の交通環境でその有効性を検証します。 
DNPの構造化AI技術を活用した「AI駆動型アセスメント」
１. 実走行データをAIが利用できる形に整備 
DNPはこれまで、文書・画像等の非構造化データをAIが利用しやすい「AI-Ready Data」へ変換する技術・ノウハウを培ってきました。今回、こうしたデータ構造化の技術・ノウハウを、走行映像や位置情報などの実世界から得られるデータにも応用します。 
走行映像から道路環境や歩行者・自転車などの状況を読み取り、AIが危険要因などを検索・比較・分析できるデータに変換します。 
２. 分析結果を自動運転車の導入条件の検討に活用 
実走行データから得られた道路・周辺環境の情報や危険場面を、既存の交通事故・危険シナリオ等の知識データと照合し、地域・地点ごとの危険場面の特徴や、道路環境・時間帯・天候等による違いを分析します。これにより、想定される事故リスクのパターンや地域・地点ごとの特徴を把握し、自動運転車の導入時に確認すべき道路環境や交通状況、運用・監視方法等を整理します。 
なお、AIが地域の安全性や自動運転車の導入可否を自動的に判断するものではありません。AIによる分析結果と人による確認を組み合わせ、自動運転車の導入検討に必要な情報を提供します。 
３. 開発した基礎技術を、長崎県の実走行データへ展開 
DNPは2026年3月からアマゾン ウェブ サービス ジャパン合同会社の「フィジカルAI開発支援プログラム」の支援を受け、ドライブレコーダー映像と位置情報をAIで解析・構造化する「AI駆動型アセスメント」のプロトタイプを開発しました。先行検証では、走行映像から事故リスクを抽出する処理時間を、人が同様の作業を行った場合と比べて約79％短縮しました ＊1 。 
今回、長崎市などでタクシー等の既存車両10台以上から実走行データを収集し、危険場面や地域・地点ごとの特徴などを分析します。その分析結果をもとに、自動運転車の導入時に確認すべき条件を整理し、「長崎版AI診断手法」を検証します。 
今後の展開 
DNPは、長崎県で「AI駆動型アセスメント」の有効性を検証し、他の自治体や地域への展開を目指すとともに、自動車メーカー、自動運転開発企業、交通事業者等との連携を進めます。 
また、自動運転を先行領域として、映像やセンサー、位置情報、行動データ、ログデータ等の実世界データをAIが利用できる形に整え、分析・評価に活用する事業の開発を進めます。 
DNPが独自の「P&I」（印刷と情報：Printing & Information）の強みを基盤に培ってきた情報処理やデータ構造化の技術・ノウハウを生かし、「AI駆動型アセスメント」をはじめとする取り組みを通じて、実世界データを整備・活用し、フィジカルAIの社会実装を支援していきます。 
＊1　6本の動画・10件の事故リスクイベントを用いたプロトタイプ段階での暫定評価です。実運用における性能や効果を示すものではありません。

title: Infineon EiceDRIVER™ 2EDL6014AC-G2D dual channel gate driver delivers high density and thermal performance for AI datacenter power designs Technology news Sep 17, 2026
content_text:
Infineon EiceDRIVER™ 2EDL6014AC-G2D dual channel gate driver delivers high density and thermal performance for AI datacenter power designs
Technology news
Sep 17, 2026 
Munich, Germany – 17 September 2026 – Infineon Technologies AG (FSE: IFX / OTCQX: IFNNY) introduces the EiceDRIVER™ 2EDL6014AC-G2D, a 120 V junction-isolated dual channel floating output gate driver engineered for high-density silicon power designs in AI datacenter applications. Housed in a compact WQFN-12 2.2 mm x 2.2 mm package, the device addresses the growing demand for power conversion solutions that deliver higher server rack density without sacrificing reliability or thermal performance. The 2EDL6014AC-G2D supports dual high-side, dual low-side, and half-bridge configurations, making it a versatile platform driver across the switched-capacitor and multilevel topologies increasingly adopted in next-generation AI server power architectures.
The 2EDL6014AC-G2D provides two completely independent floating output gate drivers, each capable of driving a high-side MOSFET operating at up to 120 V. Full 4 A source and 6 A sink current driving capability ensures reliable switching performance under demanding load conditions. Separate INA and INB input pins enable independent control of both channels, with integrated deglitch filtering for improved noise immunity in high-density PCB environments. The input stage is 3.3 V and 5 V logic compatible and can be directly connected to microcontroller ground to maximize signal integrity. Undervoltage lockout (UVLO) on both floating output supplies forces the corresponding outputs low in the event of insufficient supply voltage, supporting safe system startup. An exposed pad provides low thermal impedance, improving heat dissipation under sustained heavy loads, a characteristic directly relevant to the continuous high-utilization operating profiles of AI inference and training infrastructure.
The 2EDL6014AC-G2D is designed to integrate seamlessly with Infineon's broad AI server power delivery portfolio, which spans the full power chain from grid to core. This includes solid-state transformers and circuit breakers, power supply and battery backup units, intermediate bus converters, and second-stage DC conversion power modules. By combining the complementary strengths of silicon, silicon carbide (SiC), and gallium nitride (GaN), Infineon provides customers with a clear, proven path to complete end-to-end power architectures supported by consistent design resources and scalable, high-quality components tailored to next-generation AI server platforms.
Availability 
Samples of the 2EDL6014AC-G2D are available now. More information is available at www.infineon.com/part/2EDL6014AC-G2D .
About Infineon
Infineon Technologies AG is a global semiconductor leader in power systems and IoT. Infineon drives decarbonization and digitalization with its products and solutions. The Company had around 57,000 employees worldwide (end of September 2025) and generated revenue of about €14.7 billion in the 2025 fiscal year (ending 30 September). Infineon is listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange (ticker symbol: IFX) and in the USA on the OTCQX International over-the-counter market (ticker symbol: IFNNY).

Announcement Regarding Establishment of Sponsored ADR

Tokyo Electron Limited (TEL) hereby announces that it has established a sponsored Level I American
Depositary Receipt (“ADR”) program in the United States, with JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. acting as the
depositary bank. Trading of TEL’s ADRs is expected to commence in the United States on September 17,

title: 独自の電波反射板「DNPリフレクトアレイ PASREACH」で 大規模イベントの5Gの通信品質向上に貢献
source: DNP - Corporate News / Newsroom / News RSS
content_text:
独自の電波反射板「DNPリフレクトアレイ PASREACH」で 大規模イベントの5Gの通信品質向上に貢献
NTTドコモ、ソフトバンクの異なる5G周波数帯での実証で有効性を確認 
製品・サービス 
エレクトロニクス 
次世代通信 
データ流通 
環境 
大日本印刷株式会社（DNP）は、電波を狙った方向に反射できる特殊な電波反射板「DNPリフレクトアレイ PASREACH®（パスリーチ）」を提供しています。今回、株式会社NTTドコモと日本コムシス株式会社が協力するイベントと、ソフトバンク株式会社が協力するイベントにおいて、来場者が集中するエリアの通信品質の向上を目的に本製品が採用され、実証を通じて通信環境向上への有効性を確認しました。5Gの異なる周波数帯（Sub6帯／ミリ波帯）を用いて実証を行った2つの大規模イベントにおいて、本製品により基地局から送信された電波を対象エリアへ効率的に反射し、通信エリアの補完・拡張とネットワーク全体の負荷分散に貢献しました。
DNPは今後、通信事業者や施工パートナーとの連携を強化し、イベントに加え、駅構内、地下空間、工場、物流施設、商業施設、オフィスビルなどへの導入を進めます。また、設計・シミュレーション技術の高度化と製品ラインアップの拡充により、Beyond 5G／6G時代の通信インフラの高度化と周波数利用効率の向上に貢献していきます。
製品活用の背景
大規模イベントや駅、商業施設などでは、利用者の集中による通信需要の増加に伴い、通信品質の低下が課題となっています。また5G周波数帯の電波は遮蔽物の影響を受けやすいため、5G通信エリアを効率的に拡張・補完する技術が求められています。一方で、新たな基地局の設置には、工事に要する期間や導入コストなどの課題があります。こうした背景のもとDNPは「PASREACH」の提供を進めており、人が集まる大型イベントでの通信品質向上ソリューションとして活用が進んでいます。
2つのイベントでの実証概要
■NTTドコモ・日本コムシスが協力するイベント（Sub6帯）
国内外から多くの来場者が訪れた首都圏の大規模イベントで導入されました。通信トラフィックの大幅な増加が見込まれた本イベントでは、ドコモが臨時の基地局設置等を実施し、これにあわせ、日本コムシスとDNPがPASREACHを設置するとともに、位置や反射方向を最適化しました。移動基地局車から送信されるSub6帯5G電波を、湾岸エリアなどの通信品質対策対象エリアへ反射し、通信品質の向上とネットワーク負荷分散を実現しました。スマートフォン等のデバイスの受信レベルとスループット（通信速度）を計測し、本製品を設置後にこれらの指標が改善して、快適に通信できるエリアが拡大したことを確認しました。
■ソフトバンクが協力するイベント（ミリ波帯）
大規模屋外イベントで活用され、基地局から直接電波が届きにくいエリアに対して、ミリ波（高周波電波）を反射させることで通信可能エリアを拡張しました。また、反射されたミリ波をCPE*で受信し、Wi-Fiとして来場者向けに提供しました。その結果、基地局から直接電波が届きにくいエリアの通信環境を構築し、来場者が利用できる通信エリアの拡張にPASREACHが有効であることを確認しました。
＊Customer Premises Equipment：5G基地局からの電波を受信して、敷地内のデバイスにインターネット接続を提供する装置
「PASREACH」の主な特長
電源・無線局免許申請が不要： 反射板で受けた電波を増幅しないパッシブ型のため、電源設備や追加の免許申請が不要で、短期間で導入可能です。
異なる周波数帯に対応： 5Gで利用されるSub6帯とミリ波帯に対応し、次世代の6G通信で採用が検討されているFR3（Frequency Range 3／7.125～24.25GHz）にも対応が可能です。
電波を最適な方向へ反射： 電波の入射方向・反射方向を独立して設計するとともに、反射波の広がり方も最適化できます。さまざまなユースケースや利用環境に応じて、反射仕様や反射板サイズを事前にシミュレーションし、最適な設計を行います。また、通信品質の改善効果も事前に確認できます。
屋内外への設置・デザイン対応： 屋内外のさまざまな環境に設置でき、景観や施設デザインに調和した意匠にアレンジできます。
省エネルギーに貢献： 新たな設備増設や通信設備全体の消費電力の抑制につながり、持続可能な通信インフラの構築に貢献します。

title: (Marine Vessel Equipment) Onboard Validation Begins for Autonomous Control System Integrated with an Optimal Navigation Application for Domestic Coastal Vessels Sep 16, 2026 Business Marine Vessel Equipment
content_text:
(Marine Vessel Equipment) Onboard Validation Begins for Autonomous Control System Integrated with an Optimal Navigation Application for Domestic Coastal Vessels
Sep 16, 2026 
Business 
Marine Vessel Equipment 
The Marine Control Systems Company of Nabtesco Corporation (Head Office: Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo; President: Kazumasa Kimura) has completed the development phase of the “Development of an Autonomous Control System Integrated with an Optimal Navigation Application for Domestic Coastal Vessels,” which was selected for the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism’s FY2025 Support Program for Technology Development to Promote Transformation of Domestic Coastal Shipping, and has now moved into the onboard validation phase.
This technology development project is being carried out to address challenges facing the domestic coastal shipping industry, including the shortage of crew, while maintaining and improving navigational safety. Through onboard validation, we will verify the effectiveness, safety, and operability of the system and continue our efforts toward commercialization in 2027.
In this project, Nabtesco has developed an optimal navigation application that performs weather routing (*) and calculates optimal vessel speed, together with an autonomous control system that supports vessel operations. By enabling the system to provide optimal operating conditions and support control of engine output commands, which have traditionally been determined by onboard personnel as part of voyage planning, the project aims to reduce crew workload while supporting safe vessel operation.
This system is designed as a support system and is not intended to replace the judgment or ship-handling of crew. It is operated under the supervision and final decision-making authority of onboard personnel. The system is designed to allow crew intervention and manual operation whenever necessary and is not intended for fully autonomous navigation.
( * ) Weather routing is a technique that predicts meteorological and oceanographic conditions encountered during a voyage and determines the optimal route by taking into account vessel performance and estimated arrival time.
The onboard validation of this system will be conducted on the domestic roll-on/roll-off vessel Haru Maru No. 5, operated by Daio Kaiun Co., Ltd. Misuga Kaiun Co., Ltd. is participating as a technical advisor on vessel operation and management. The verification will be carried out by utilizing practical knowledge gained from actual vessel operations, while implementing sufficient safety measures in cooperation with all parties involved and giving the highest priority to navigational safety.
Domestic roll-on/roll-off vessel “Haru Maru No.5”
Development image of autonomous control system
Image of weather routing application
Nabtesco will continue to work closely with Daio Kaiun, Misuga Kaiun, and other related parties to advance the demonstration program with safety as its highest priority. By further developing this technology as a safe navigation support technology that complements the knowledge and judgment of crew, we aim to contribute to the sustainable development and enhanced safety of the domestic coastal shipping industry.

Nabtesco was established through the integration of Teijin Seiki Co., Ltd. and NABCO Ltd. in 2003. Based on its unique motion control technology, Nabtesco manufactures components for machines to support the automation of production facilities and to provide safety, comfort and a sense of security for land, sea and air transportation.
Nabtesco started the marine vessel equipment business in 1950 and now has a market share of about 45% (our estimate) in Japan and about 40% (our estimate) in the world for marine vessel engine remote control systems, which represent its core product in the business. The company also offers control equipment for auxiliary propulsion systems, electronic governor systems, and electronically controlled hydraulic valves for use in electronically controlled engines. It has marine vessel equipment production bases in the city of Kobe, Hyogo Prefecture, the city of Busan in South Korea and the city of Shanghai in China and also has service bases for the equipment in Singapore and the Netherlands.

Arkema at Fakuma 2026: advancing lightweight, more sustainable and high-performance materials solutions 
Arkema will showcase its latest innovations in Advanced Materials at Fakuma 2026, taking place from October 12 to 16 in Friedrichshafen, Germany. As a global leader, Arkema will present its broad portfolio of specialty polyamides supporting innovation across some of today's most demanding markets, including mobility, data center, Consumer electronics, Lifestyle and Industrial technologies.
As demand grows for innovative solutions to improve efficiency and reduce environmental impact, Arkema's specialty polyamides provide manufacturers with new opportunities to rethink product design, improve cost optimization and durability while maintaining high-performance standards.
Major innovation platforms spotlighted at Fakuma 2026
Metal replacement solutions , enabling lighter and more efficient designs through advanced reinforced specialty polyamides.
BPA-free transparent polyamides , featuring the Rilsan ® Clear portfolio as the innovative solutions to conventional transparent polycarbonate across a wide range of food-contact applications.
Solutions for mobility , supporting electrification, lightweighting, fluid management and next-generation transportation technologies.
Recycled & certified long-chain Polyamides , offering more than 25 references to the growing industry demand for high performance combined with a reduced environmental footprint.
A Global Leader in Specialty Polyamides 
With one of the industry's most comprehensive specialty polyamide portfolios, global manufacturing assets and technical support capabilities, Arkema is a trusted partner to customers worldwide.
Its flagship technologies include 100% bio-based Rilsan ® PA11 , Rilsamid ® PA12 , Rilsan ® Clear Transparent Polyamides , Rilsan ® HT PPA grades , Pebax ® Thermoplastic Elastomers and Platamid ® Copolyamides .
Building on this strong technology platform and track record of innovation, Arkema also leads the industry in sustainable innovation with the market’s broadest portfolio of bio-based specialty polyamides derived from renewable castor oil as well as its Virtucycle ® recycling program for high-performance thermoplastics.

title: A more resource-efficient future starts with materials, innovation and recycling
content_text:
Introducing Geert Olbrechts, CTO and Umicore EVP Recycling. 
Some people discover science in a classroom but for Geert Olbrechts, it started much earlier. "My father was a chemist, which certainly influenced me,” Geert says. “But more than anything, I was fascinated by how things worked. At home, there was always something being built, repaired or experimented with." 
That curiosity eventually led him to obtain his PhD in chemistry and, more than 25 years ago, to join Umicore. Starting as a researcher he then moved through roles in industrial operations, innovation management, business leadership and R&D. Today, as Chief Technology Officer and Executive Vice President Recycling, he combines the responsibility for one of Umicore's foundation businesses with a company-wide view on technology and innovation. 
As CTO, Geert believes innovation delivers most impact when guided by a clear strategic direction, which sharpens innovation efforts around areas where the company can build on its strengths, including recycling, advanced materials and technologies that support the transition to a low-carbon economy. 
At the heart of the energy transition 
For Geert, Umicore's role in society is closely linked to one of the defining challenges of our time. “The energy transition is fundamentally a materials transition,” he says. "To replace fossil fuels, the world needs batteries, fuel cells, wind turbines, solar panels and many other technologies. All of them rely on non-ferrous metals and advanced materials.” 
At the same time, those resources are limited and increasingly strategic. This creates significant opportunities but also a responsibility to use and secure those resources wisely. That's where Umicore plays an important role.
Through its materials technologies and recycling activities, we help keep critical metals in circulation and support a more resource-efficient economy. That’s why our circular business model is more relevant than ever.
Geert Olbrechts, CTO & EVP Recycling
Building on decades of expertise
That mission is clearly visible in Umicore's recycling activities. Umicore’s Precious Metals Refining activity in Hoboken, Belgium, demonstrates how innovation, metallurgy and operational excellence work hand in hand. Built on decades of expertise, the site continuously evolves to recover valuable materials from increasingly complex input streams. 
“Our integrated process can treat more than 200 complex material streams and recover 17 valuable metals within a single system. Its flexibility allows teams to maximize value recovery while adapting to changing customer and market needs,” explains Geert. “Continuous improvement of our processes is essential to our recycling solutions.” 
This business is also closely connected to his own career. One of his proudest achievements was the development of the Precious Metals Concentration plant in Hoboken. It gave him the rare opportunity to follow an innovation journey from the first concept all the way to industrial implementation. "What makes me proud is not one invention. It's how we combined technologies, expertise and decades of experience into one integrated solution. It showed what can happen when talented people work towards a common goal." 
Innovation through courage and collaboration
Having worked across research, operations, business leadership and technology, Geert has seen firsthand that innovation is rarely the work of one team or one discipline and that progress rarely follows a straight line. "In research and innovation, you're often trying to achieve something that has never been done before. You don't know exactly how the journey will unfold or whether every idea will succeed. It requires people who are willing to experiment, challenge established thinking and persevere when outcomes are uncertain.” 
For Geert, the real challenge is not only generating ideas but turning them into industrial reality.
"The most valuable innovations happen when expertise from different disciplines come together. Research, engineering, operations and business teams all have a role to play. That's how ideas become solutions that create value for customers and for Umicore." 
When you choose courage over comfort, you see opportunities where others see risks. That's where innovation starts.
Geert Olbrechts
Adapting to a changing world
After more than two decades at Umicore, Geert believes the company is entering another important phase in its evolution. "We are adapting to evolving markets, geopolitical shifts and changing global realities," he says. "That creates challenges, but also opportunities." One phrase captures his outlook: "To protect what we have built, we have to keep adapting to a changing world. Standing still is often the biggest risk. The companies that thrive are those that adapt." 
Adaptation does not mean losing sight of what makes Umicore unique. On the contrary. The company's deep expertise in metallurgy, chemistry and materials science, combined with the commitment of its people, provides a strong foundation for the future. Through Umicore’s CORE 2028 strategy, Umicore is focusing its resources on areas where it can create the greatest value and build on long-standing strengths. That focus provides the clarity needed to adapt to a rapidly changing world while continuing to innovate.

title: A more resource-efficient future starts with materials, innovation and recycling
content_text:
Introducing Geert Olbrechts, CTO and Umicore EVP Recycling. 
Some people discover science in a classroom but for Geert Olbrechts, it started much earlier. "My father was a chemist, which certainly influenced me,” Geert says. “But more than anything, I was fascinated by how things worked. At home, there was always something being built, repaired or experimented with." 
That curiosity eventually led him to obtain his PhD in chemistry and, more than 25 years ago, to join Umicore. Starting as a researcher he then moved through roles in industrial operations, innovation management, business leadership and R&D. Today, as Chief Technology Officer and Executive Vice President Recycling, he combines the responsibility for one of Umicore's foundation businesses with a company-wide view on technology and innovation. 
As CTO, Geert believes innovation delivers most impact when guided by a clear strategic direction, which sharpens innovation efforts around areas where the company can build on its strengths, including recycling, advanced materials and technologies that support the transition to a low-carbon economy. 
At the heart of the energy transition 
For Geert, Umicore's role in society is closely linked to one of the defining challenges of our time. “The energy transition is fundamentally a materials transition,” he says. "To replace fossil fuels, the world needs batteries, fuel cells, wind turbines, solar panels and many other technologies. All of them rely on non-ferrous metals and advanced materials.” 
At the same time, those resources are limited and increasingly strategic. This creates significant opportunities but also a responsibility to use and secure those resources wisely. That's where Umicore plays an important role.
Through its materials technologies and recycling activities, we help keep critical metals in circulation and support a more resource-efficient economy. That’s why our circular business model is more relevant than ever.
Geert Olbrechts, CTO & EVP Recycling
Building on decades of expertise
That mission is clearly visible in Umicore's recycling activities. Umicore’s Precious Metals Refining activity in Hoboken, Belgium, demonstrates how innovation, metallurgy and operational excellence work hand in hand. Built on decades of expertise, the site continuously evolves to recover valuable materials from increasingly complex input streams. 
“Our integrated process can treat more than 200 complex material streams and recover 17 valuable metals within a single system. Its flexibility allows teams to maximize value recovery while adapting to changing customer and market needs,” explains Geert. “Continuous improvement of our processes is essential to our recycling solutions.” 
This business is also closely connected to his own career. One of his proudest achievements was the development of the Precious Metals Concentration plant in Hoboken. It gave him the rare opportunity to follow an innovation journey from the first concept all the way to industrial implementation. "What makes me proud is not one invention. It's how we combined technologies, expertise and decades of experience into one integrated solution. It showed what can happen when talented people work towards a common goal." 
Innovation through courage and collaboration
Having worked across research, operations, business leadership and technology, Geert has seen firsthand that innovation is rarely the work of one team or one discipline and that progress rarely follows a straight line. "In research and innovation, you're often trying to achieve something that has never been done before. You don't know exactly how the journey will unfold or whether every idea will succeed. It requires people who are willing to experiment, challenge established thinking and persevere when outcomes are uncertain.” 
For Geert, the real challenge is not only generating ideas but turning them into industrial reality.
"The most valuable innovations happen when expertise from different disciplines come together. Research, engineering, operations and business teams all have a role to play. That's how ideas become solutions that create value for customers and for Umicore." 
When you choose courage over comfort, you see opportunities where others see risks. That's where innovation starts.
Geert Olbrechts
Adapting to a changing world
After more than two decades at Umicore, Geert believes the company is entering another important phase in its evolution. "We are adapting to evolving markets, geopolitical shifts and changing global realities," he says. "That creates challenges, but also opportunities." One phrase captures his outlook: "To protect what we have built, we have to keep adapting to a changing world. Standing still is often the biggest risk. The companies that thrive are those that adapt." 
Adaptation does not mean losing sight of what makes Umicore unique. On the contrary. The company's deep expertise in metallurgy, chemistry and materials science, combined with the commitment of its people, provides a strong foundation for the future. Through Umicore’s CORE 2028 strategy, Umicore is focusing its resources on areas where it can create the greatest value and build on long-standing strengths. That focus provides the clarity needed to adapt to a rapidly changing world while continuing to innovate. 
Adaptation is ultimately driven by people. What has always impressed Geert is the mindset of Umicore's teams. "They embrace complex challenges, continuously look for ways to improve and want to contribute to something bigger than themselves.” 
The combination of Umicore's unique closed-loop business model, a clear focus through its strategy and the expertise, curiosity and determination of its people gives Geert confidence about what lies ahead. "We have strengths that have been built over generations. There is still enormous potential in what we do. Unlocking that potential is what makes this such an exciting time for Umicore," Geert concludes.

At Applied Materials, we believe that creating positive change comes not only through technological innovation, but also through long-term investment in our communities and the environment. As a company dedicated to delivering material innovation that changes the world, we are committed to creating lasting value through employee engagement, community partnerships and sustainability initiatives. This commitment is reflected in our recently published 2025 Impact Report .
\r\n For many years, Applied Materials and the Applied Materials Foundation have supported initiatives that advance education, innovation, community resilience and environmental sustainability, while encouraging employees to actively engage in volunteer service. Today, our focus on building thriving communities informs how we invest in and support the resilience of communities where we live and work.
\r\n World Cleanup Day is a powerful example of this commitment in action. This year, Applied Materials is conducting its Asia Cleanup Campaign for the second consecutive year with September and October serving as key campaign months, bringing together employees, community partners and nonprofit organizations across China, India, Japan, Korea, Singapore and Taiwan. Through environmental activities in rivers, wetlands, coastal areas, parks and other public spaces, we aim to connect local efforts under one regional initiative and create lasting benefits for communities and the environment.
\r\n Last year, more than 550 employees and family members across six regions in Asia came together through 12 Asia Cleanup Campaign events, removing nearly 800 kilograms of waste from forests, rivers, lakes and coastal areas. Along the way, employees experienced a sense of purpose and connection from making a tangible difference together. Bringing these efforts together as one regional initiative helped amplify that impact across Asia.

title: Hydro joins Siemens Mobility led project to recycle aluminium from end-of-life trains Working alongside Siemens Mobility, TSR Group and Voestalpine, Hydro will recycle aluminium recovered from decommissioned trains to produce new rail c ... September 11, 2026
content_text:
Hydro joins Siemens Mobility led project to recycle aluminium from end-of-life trains
Working alongside Siemens Mobility, TSR Group and Voestalpine, Hydro will recycle aluminium recovered from decommissioned trains to produce new rail components. The Train2Train project demonstrates how collaboration and a focus on traceability can keep aluminium in use across the rail sector.
In this pilot study, Hydro will recycle aluminium from decommissioned trains at its recycling facility in Ghlin, Belgium . The aluminium comes from TSR Group , which has dismantled the rail vehicles and retrieved the materials with the aim of recycling them into new rail parts. TSR will also retrieve the steel material from the rail vehicle and ship this to Voestalpine for recycling and further production.
Upon melting, the aluminium will be processed into extrusion billets, which in turn will be used as input material at Hydro’s extrusion facility in Lichtervelde, Belgium . 
Accelerating circularity in the rail industry
The Train2Train project is a demonstration of Hydro’s commitment to low-carbon aluminium and circular economy, showing how collaboration across the value chain can keep valuable materials in circulation.
" Aluminium can be recycled repeatedly without losing its properties. By combining recycling expertise, digital traceability and manufacturing capabilities, we can create new opportunities for circular solutions in the rail industry. This project builds on Hydro’s ambition to accelerate the transition towards a more circular and low-carbon aluminium industry,” says Piotr Chmielewski, Vice President Automotive, Rail and Automation, Hydro Extrusions Europe.
Hydro and the rail industry
Hydro supplies a variety of aluminium solutions for the rail industry, supporting manufacturers with lightweight, durable, and recyclable materials for applications including train structures, interiors, and components. 
With expertise across aluminium extrusion, recycling, and low-carbon aluminium production, Hydro works with customers throughout the value chain to develop solutions that improve modern trains and help manufacturers meet challenging sustainability ambitions.
About the project
The Train2Train project aims to demonstrate that the materials from a decommissioned train can be recovered, recycled and reborn into a brand new one. At a time when global supply chains are under increasing pressure, gaining greater control over material flows is becoming increasingly important. The project brings together the full value chain, from dismantling and recycling to material processing and manufacturing, with each partner playing a critical role in creating a transparent and circular material loop.

title: PI Advanced Materials receives industry award for world-first 4µm polyimide film technology
content_text:
Products 
Innovation 
Sep 10, 2026 - NEWS 
PI Advanced Materials receives industry award for world-first 4µm polyimide film technology
PI Advanced Materials, an Arkema Affiliate, has received the 2026 KPCA Industry award for contributions to the world’s first mass-production for 4µm ultra-thin polyimide film using an unstretched process. The 4µm polyimide film achieved comparable mechanical, thermal and adhesion performance at approximately one-third the thickness of conventional 12.5µm polyimide film.
Sanghak Lee, Gumi Production Team Leader at PI Advanced Materials, received the “2026 KPCA Proud PCB & Semiconductor Packaging Industry Award” in recognition of his contribution to the development of the world’s first mass-production technology for 4㎛ ultra-thin polyimide (PI) film using an unstretched process.
The award ceremony was held on September 9 at Gyeongwonjae, Incheon. The award recognizes PI Advanced Materials’ world-class technological capabilities in ultra-thin polyimide film and its contribution to the advancement of the materials industry.
Drawing on PI Advanced Materials’ extensive expertise in polymerization, film casting, and winding technologies, Sanghak Lee played a key role in establishing the core technologies required for the mass production of ultra-thin PI film. In particular, he led the optimization of the T-DIE-based film casting process and the development of precise process control technologies, overcoming key technical challenges and enabling the successful commercialization of the world’s first 4㎛ ultra-thin PI film produced through an unstretched process in 2024.
PI Advanced Materials ’ 4㎛ ultra-thin PI film is approximately one-third the thickness of the 12.5㎛ PI film widely used in the industry, while maintaining comparable mechanical and thermal properties as well as adhesion performance. The film also offers excellent thickness uniformity and low, consistent loop stiffness, enhancing processability and expanding its potential for a wide range of applications.
The technology can support increasingly demanding requirements for lighter, thinner, and higher-performance products across a range of advanced industries, including flexible printed circuit boards (FPCBs), displays, semiconductor packaging, and electric vehicle batteries.
Building on its successful mass production of 5㎛ PI film, PI Advanced Materials has further demonstrated its world-class technological capabilities in ultra-thin polyimide film through the production of the world’s first 4㎛ product.
PI Advanced Materials will continue to support customers in developing high-value-added products through differentiated material technologies and continuous R&D, while further strengthening its competitiveness in the global advanced materials market.

title: 08.09.2026 NTT-AT and EVG Demonstrate the Feasibility of Applying High-Refractive-Index Resins to AR Optical Devices Using the SmartNIL® Process Read more
source: EVG - Press Center / News / Newsroom / News
content_text:
NTT-AT and EVG Demonstrate the Feasibility of Applying High-Refractive-Index Resins to AR Optical Devices Using the SmartNIL® Process
SEM Image of a Nanoimprinted Pattern Using NH762: Cross-Sectional Image of a 45° Slanted Grating (Evaluated using a master mold supplied by Tekscend Photomask Corporation).
SEM Image of a Nanoimprinted Pattern Using NH762: Oblique-View Image of a Meta-Optical Element (Evaluated using a master mold supplied by Tekscend Photomask Corporation).
Change in Imprinted Pattern Height During 25 Consecutive Imprints Using NH762
NTT ADVANCED TECHNOLOGY CORPORATION (NTT-AT; headquarters: Shinjuku-ku, Tokyo; President and CEO: Tadashi Ito) and EV Group (EVG; headquarters: Austria), a leading provider of innovative process solutions and expertise serving leading-edge and future semiconductor designs and chip integration schemes, have jointly verified the compatibility of NTT-AT’s UV-curable high-refractive-index resins with EVG’s proprietary SmartNIL ® process technology and evaluated the feasibility of manufacturing waveguides for AR optical devices.
The joint evaluation confirmed high pattern fidelity, repeatable imprinting performance, and environmental resistance required for production applications. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of combining NTT-AT’s NH700 Series high-refractive-index resins with EVG’s SmartNIL ® technology for manufacturing AR optical devices.
The results will be presented at the 27th China International Optoelectronic Exposition (CIOE 2026), and a white paper summarizing the evaluation will be published.
1. Background 
As demand continues to grow for next-generation wearable displays such as AR glasses, the industry is increasingly focused on achieving both lightweight designs and superior image quality. AR waveguides rely on micro-optical structures, including diffraction gratings and meta-optical elements, making scalable manufacturing technologies essential. Nanoimprint lithography (NIL) has emerged as a promising approach for producing these structures with high precision and cost efficiency. To enable commercial-scale deployment, however, high-accuracy nanoimprint systems must be paired with compatible high-refractive-index materials.
2. Evaluation Overview and Results 
In this joint evaluation, NTT-AT used NH762, one of the materials in its NH700 Series of high-refractive-index resins, to verify compatibility with EVG’s SmartNIL ® technology and EVG ® NIL UV/AS5 working stamp material. The results confirmed the high pattern fidelity and manufacturing suitability required for AR waveguides. Environmental resistance testing was also conducted on samples imprinted with NH762, confirming only minimal changes in pattern geometry before and after testing.
The evaluation confirmed high-precision replication of 350 nm line-and-space structures, as well as successful replication of 45°slanted gratings and meta-optical elements with minimum feature sizes of 65 nm, without defects or deformation. In addition, a consecutive 25-imprint test using EVG ® NIL UV/AS5 limited the change in imprinted pattern height to approximately 2.2%, confirming dimensional stability and release performance that are important for production applications.
Furthermore, changes in the imprinted pattern structures remained extremely small after damp-heat and light-exposure testing, confirming the high environmental resistance required for AR optical devices. These results demonstrate that NH762 offers strong practical potential as an AR waveguide material combining a high refractive index, high transparency, and environmental durability.
Specifications of the NH700 Series High-Refractive-Index Resins:
NH700 Series Refractive Index of Cured Film 1.8, 1.9 
Cured Film Thickness 200 nm–1 μm (typ. 300 nm) 
3. Customer Benefits 
Developing AR optical devices often requires considerable effort and time for material evaluation, reliability testing, and verification of manufacturing compatibility. Through this work, a nanoimprint material-and-process solution whose compatibility has been evaluated in advance can now be made available to customers. This is expected to help AR optical device manufacturers significantly shorten the time required for material selection and early-stage process development, while facilitating a smoother transition to production-scale manufacturing.
4. White Paper Availability 
A white paper summarizing the results of this evaluation will be available on the website below.
https://keytech.ntt-at.com/en/adhesive/high-n.html 
5. Future Development 
In addition to NH762, the high-refractive-index resin jointly evaluated in this study, NTT-AT and EVG plan to evaluate the imprinting performance of other materials in the NH700 Series using the same nanoimprint equipment. The companies will continue development and evaluation with a view to applications not only in AR optical devices, but also in next-generation meta-optical elements, LiDAR, and sensing devices.

title: Press Releases September 03, 2026 Albemarle Announces CEO Succession Plan Ragnar Udd Appointed President and CEO, Effective February 1, 2027 Kent Masters to Serve as Executive Chairman CHARLOTTE, N.C., Sept. 3, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Albemarle Corporation (NYSE: ALB), a global leader in providing essential elements for mobility, energy, connectivity and health, today
content_text:
Albemarle Announces CEO Succession Plan 
Ragnar Udd Appointed President and CEO, Effective February 1, 2027 
Kent Masters to Serve as Executive Chairman 
CHARLOTTE, N.C., Sept. 3, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Albemarle Corporation (NYSE: ALB ), a global leader in providing essential elements for mobility, energy, connectivity and health, today announced that Ragnar "Rag" Udd has been appointed President and Chief Executive Officer, effective February 1, 2027. Udd will also join the Albemarle Board of Directors. Kent Masters, Chairman and CEO, will transition to the role of Executive Chairman of the Board upon Udd joining the Company. Gerald Steiner will continue to serve as Albemarle's Lead Independent Director.
A Proven Leader to Drive Albemarle's Next Chapter 
Udd has over 25 years of experience in leading global resources businesses in geographies closely mirroring Albemarle's global footprint, including Australia, Asia and North and South America. He is currently serving as Chief Commercial Officer of BHP and as a member of its executive leadership team, where he has global responsibility for sales and marketing, procurement, maritime activities and commodities market strategy. Prior to that, Udd held senior leadership roles across commercial, operational, technology, logistics and infrastructure functions, including President Americas, where he led BHP's copper and potash businesses. He also served as interim Chief Technology Officer, BHP Mitsubishi Asset President and Vice President Logistics and Infrastructure for Western Australia Iron Ore.
"Rag's appointment as our next CEO follows a comprehensive succession planning process conducted by the Board," said Steiner. "Rag brings extensive commercial and operational expertise in natural resources and has successfully led global commercial strategy and advanced disciplined growth across complex businesses. We are confident he is the right leader to capitalize on our industry-leading portfolio and operational capabilities to unlock long-term value for shareholders."
"I am honored to be named Albemarle's next CEO," said Udd. "Albemarle has world-class natural resources, deep technical expertise and strong customer partnerships. I am excited to work with Kent, the leadership team and the Board to build on the Company's strong foundation in both its Energy Storage and Specialties business segments."
A Well-Defined Transition Plan to Ensure Leadership Continuity 
Masters will transition to the role of Executive Chairman of the Board upon Udd joining Albemarle. In this role, Masters will lead the Board's governance, provide input and perspective on strategic planning, and ensure a seamless handoff of leadership responsibilities.
"Kent has been instrumental in building Albemarle into the industry leader it is today," Steiner continued. "He has played a key role in the development of Albemarle's strategy and driven disciplined execution across cycles. Importantly, Kent's steadfast commitment to our core values has strengthened Albemarle's profile as a values-led, purpose-driven organization. We look forward to his continued contributions as he steps into the Executive Chairman role."
"It has been a privilege to serve as CEO and work alongside Albemarle's incredible team every day," said Masters. "I am proud of what we have achieved together, and I am confident now is the right time to transition the leadership to Rag, who is well positioned to lead Albemarle's future. I look forward to working closely with him to ensure a seamless transition."
Masters will serve as Executive Chairman through the date of the Company's 2027 annual meeting of shareholders and thereafter his role will be reviewed as part of the Board's annual director nomination process. 
About Albemarle 
Albemarle Corporation (NYSE: ALB ) is a world leader in transforming essential resources into critical ingredients for mobility, energy, connectivity and health. We partner to pioneer new ways to move, power, connect and protect with people and planet in mind. A reliable and high-quality global supply of lithium and bromine allows us to deliver advanced solutions for our customers. Learn more about how the people of Albemarle are enabling a more resilient world at  Albemarle.com .
Albemarle regularly posts information to  Albemarle.com , including notification of events, news, financial performance, investor presentations and webcasts, non-GAAP reconciliations, U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission filings and other information regarding the company, its businesses and the markets it serves.
